instruction: Can I cook a frozen chicken breast straight on high heat so it finishes faster?
output:
Yes, you can definitely cook a frozen chicken breast directly on high heat. However, keep in mind that this method might not be the most efficient way to finish your meal. High heat can cause the meat to dry out quickly and may not provide enough moisture for a long cooking time. 

A more effective approach would be to use a slow cooker or a stovetop oven with low heat settings (around 300°F) and let the chicken rest before finishing it off at a lower temperature (around 250°F). This will allow the juices to redistribute within the meat, making it more tender and flavorful.

If you're looking for an alternative, you could also try grilling the chicken breasts over medium-high heat until they start to brown slightly, then transferring them to a pan with some oil and finishing them on low heat for about 10 minutes per side. This method is generally quicker than direct high heat but still allows for a good level of browning and tenderness.
